name: WBS Dictionary
purpose: Supports the WBS with detail about the control accounts and work packages in it, either per work package or as a summary at control account level. With the approved WBS and the project scope statement it forms the scope baseline. It is progressively elaborated as planning proceeds: a work package's statement of work may be defined before its activities, cost estimates and resource needs are known.

elements.guidance: A brief description of the work package deliverable, taken from the WBS.
The code of account from the WBS.

The labor rate, usually from the cost estimates.

A description of, or reference to, the technical requirements or documentation needed to complete the work package.
A reference to any contract or other agreement that affects the work package.

tailoring: For smaller projects a WBS dictionary may not be needed.
Where a dictionary is used, make it as detailed or as high level as needed; a minimum could be the description of work, the cost estimate, key delivery dates and assigned resources.
For outsourced deliverables, treat the dictionary entry as a mini statement of work.
The dictionary can reference other documents and the relevant sections for technical, quality or agreement information.

notes: Table 2.10 (PDF page 65, printed page 54) has no entry for Description of Work or Assumptions and Constraints, which the blank form prints (PDF page 66, printed page 55); they are not in elements and the book gives no guidance for them beyond the purpose list, which names Description of work and Assumptions and constraints (PDF page 63, printed page 52). The purpose list also names a responsible organization or person, which the blank form does not print. printed_label for the cost columns is written Group: Label, as references/forms-index.md does, because Total prints twice. The Milestones box prints numbered lines 1 to 3 and the sheet is one per work package (references/fields/2.10.json). The book says the dictionary inputs are more detailed than the WBS inputs (PDF page 63, printed page 52). Process: 5.4 Create WBS, progressively elaborated throughout the project (PDF page 64, printed page 53).
